title: Consolidating Strategies for Countering Hate Speech Using Persuasive Dialogues
benchmark_measurement: Generation of persuasive counter-arguments against hate speech targeting religious groups (Muslims and Jews). The evaluation focused on the quality of the generated responses in terms of fluency, argumentativeness, and logical soundness.
findings: The paper's findings are not specific to religion but to the general task of countering hate speech. The study found that generating convincing counter-arguments, including those against religious hate speech, is most effective when the generation model is controlled using a combination of value-based features (like Big-5 personality traits) and structure-based features (like argument schemes). This combination performed better than using no features or other combinations of features.
